Name: PADDR[6:2]
Structural Path: PADDR[6:2] -> s_apb_addr -> PADDIR/GPIOLOCK decode -> protected-write acceptance -> gpio_dir
Attack Scenarios: Changing the decoded APB address can redirect a transaction to PADDIR or GPIOLOCK and enable an otherwise denied direction update.
Justification: Attacker-controlled address bits select the direction register; the de-aliased address path was dynamically controllable.

Name: PWDATA[0]
Structural Path: PWDATA[0] -> GPIOLOCK write data -> r_gpio_lock[0] -> PADDIR authorization -> gpio_dir
Attack Scenarios: Changing the GPIOLOCK data bit can prevent lock establishment or create an unlock state before a protected PADDIR write.
Justification: The untrusted APB write-data bit directly determines the unauthorized direction value.

Name: r_gpio_lock[0]
Structural Path: r_gpio_lock[0] -> PADDIR write authorization -> r_gpio_dir -> gpio_dir
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting the stored lock bit removes the authorization guard and permits a protected direction-register update.
Justification: The lock state is controllable through evaluated bus paths and gates whether a direction write is authorized.
